statement: For the SSH chain with intra-cell hopping v and inter-cell hopping w (v, w rational, nonzero, |v| != |w|): the open chain with 2N+1 sites has nullity(H) = 1 exactly, with kernel vector psi_A(n) = (-v/w)^n on A sites and 0 on B sites; the open chain with 2N sites has rank(H) = 2N exactly (no zero mode), because det(D) = v^N for its lower-bidiagonal sublattice block D. Verified on 6 rational (v,w) instances x 3 chain sizes (N = 2, 3, 5) = 18 parameter points, in exact fractions.Fraction arithmetic (no floating point).

Positive control demonstrated to fire: PC1 (v=0 decoupled-site chain triggers the zero-mode detector), guarding against a rank/nullity check that never reports a zero mode.

statement: For h(z) = v + wz on the counterclockwise unit circle |z| = 1 with |v/w| < 1 (pole inside), (1/2*pi*i) * oint h'(z)/h(z) dz = 1, by Mathlib's circleIntegral.integral_sub_inv_of_mem_ball (h'/h = (z + v/w)^-1, a simple pole at -v/w inside the ball). The case |v/w| > 1 (pole outside) is not covered by that lemma and needs Cauchy's theorem for a pole outside the contour; the exact Mathlib name for that step has not yet been identified.

statement: CORRECTED 2026-09-27 (v2). On an SSH ring of L cells (|w|>|v|, subsystem of ell whole cells severing two w-bonds), the two entanglement levels closest to 1/2 form an exact chiral pair z1+z2=1 and sit at |z-1/2| ~ (v/w)^min(ell, L-ell): ordinary exponential finite-size smearing, with decay length fitted within 15% of xi = 1/ln(w/v) at r = 0.5, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9 (L=200). They are pinned to 1/2 EXACTLY only at ell = L/2, where a reflection through the two cuts combined with chiral symmetry cancels the hybridisation. When |v|>|w| no level is near 1/2. Version 1 of this claim stated there was NO finite-size smearing and explained it as a quantised invariant that cannot smear; that was an artefact of measuring only ell = L/2 (at two ring sizes) and is retracted. Positive and negative controls stand.

statement: For the 4-body Majorana SYK model (N Majoranas, N % 4 == 0, exact diagonalization), the exact-degeneracy rate of the parity-sector ground state is a clean all-or-nothing function of N mod 8 at every tested N <= 24: 0/40 realizations degenerate at N in {8, 16, 24} (N mod 8 = 0), 40/40 at N in {12, 20} (N mod 8 = 4). statement: On layer-truncated hyperbolic {7,3} tilings vs Euclidean square/triangular disks (same node counts), the condition number of the boundary-to-bulk inverse-conductance Jacobian grows only polynomially with N for the hyperbolic case and super-polynomially (locally exp(c*depth) with depth ~ sqrt(N)) for the Euclidean case. Preregistered confirmatory point (L=4, N=847, not previously computed): predicted log10(cond) = 4.2 +/- 0.5, measured 3.89 (within band); max depth predicted 7, measured 7 (exact). At matched N~800-850, log10(cond) = 3.89 (hyperbolic) vs 11.77 (square) vs 11.71 (triangular): a 7.9-decade gap, wider than the 6.4-decade gap measured at N~315-320 in the prior exploratory pass. Unplanned but consistent finding: the hyperbolic graph stays full rank at every tested size (up to 1078/1078 at N=847), while the Euclidean graphs develop growing rank deficiency (up to 1143/3071 unidentifiable edges at N=1069).
notes: SUPERSEDED IN PART by H0-X-0002 (kappa reporting bug) and H0-B-0001 (rank-deficiency claim retracted). Kept as the record of the original, since-corrected run; not to be cited alone. experiments/track_h_hyperbolic_network/{HYPOTHESIS.md,PREREGISTRATION.md,RESULTS.md,hyperbolic_network.py} (45/45 self-test checks pass, incl. exact-vs-finite-difference Jacobian cross-check to 1.15e-11). Original HYPOTHESIS.md claimed exponential (not polynomial) edge-sensitivity decay on FLAT lattices by direct analogy to continuum Calderon-problem instability; an external reviewer showed this derivation was dimensionally inconsistent (Poisson-kernel decay is polynomial), so an unlocked exploratory pass was run before any prediction was locked, and the mechanism was revised in HYPOTHESIS.md (dated, original argument left visible) to: exponential decay in DEPTH is common to both geometries, but depth itself scales as log N (hyperbolic) vs sqrt N (flat). Real code bugs found and fixed before this result, all now caught mechanically in self_test(): boundary classification used vertex degree (misses rim-junction vertices) rather than face incidence; a triangular-lattice face had a non-adjacent vertex offset, breaking the Euler characteristic check (caught: V-E+F=-5 instead of 1); the finite-difference Jacobian's eps=1e-6 imposed a ~1e-10-relative floor on resolvable singular values, replaced by the exact harmonic-extension formula dLambda/dg_e=(P_a-P_b)^T(P_a-P_b). Novelty search bounded (2 queries): found 1107.0343 (Borcea, Druskin, Guevara Vasquez & Mamonov -- NOT 'Deban, Borcea et al.' as first mis-cited here, corrected in H0-X-0002) and 1104.4858 (Ervedoza & de Gournay); reported as 'not found in this search', not 'novel'. [EVIDENCE BLOB NOT RECOVERED: no tracked file hashes to this digest; the gate with --evidence-dir reports it. Statement unchanged.]

statement: CORRECTS H0-X-0001. The kappa this script reported was capped by its own rank-tolerance formula (kappa = s_max/s[rank-1], and s[rank-1] > tol = s_max*max(J.shape)*eps by construction, so kappa < 1/(max(J.shape)*eps) ALWAYS) -- not by float64's true precision floor, which H0-X-0001 wrongly attributed the large-N flat-lattice 'plateau' to. Verified: the reported 'saturated' log10(kappa) for the 3 largest flat cases matched log10(1/(max(J.shape)*eps)) to 4 significant figures. Corrected: kappa is now the RAW untruncated ratio s_max/s_min, and cases where s_min rounds to float64 noise are reported as NUMERICALLY SINGULAR, not as a finite number. Net effect: the corrected result is STRONGER. Points unaffected by the bug (all {7,3} L=1..4; flat lattices at N<=317) are unchanged -- the 6.4-decade gap at N~315-320 (log10 kappa 3.27 vs 9.72) stands. At N~800-850, the hyperbolic lattice remains measurable (3.89) while the flat lattice's Jacobian is correctly reported as beyond float64's ability to assign ANY condition number -- a stronger separation than a finite decade count. Also corrects a citation error: 1107.0343's authors are Borcea, Druskin, Guevara Vasquez & Mamonov, not 'Deban, Borcea et al.' as first (wrongly) attributed from a search snippet without checking papers/meta/.
notes: docs/elenchus/evidence/h0_x_0002_kappa_correction.txt. Does NOT correct the rank-deficiency claim in H0-X-0001 (a separate bug on a separate quantity) -- see H0-B-0001. statement: RETRACTS the rank-deficiency claim in H0-X-0001 (e.g. triangular N=1069: 1143/3071 'unidentifiable' edges), for the sizes tested here. Exact rank certified by modular arithmetic (GF(p), two independent primes, agreement required) over the SAME harmonic-extension Jacobian construction: {7,3} L=1 (E=42) and L=2 (E=140) are FULL RANK, certified. Flat lattices: square N=113 (E=200) and triangular N=187 (E=502) are FULL RANK, certified (agreeing with float64 at these unsaturated sizes). DECISIVE: triangular N=475 (E=1331), a size comparable to the N=421 instance float64 reported as deficient (102/1176), is EXACTLY FULL RANK, certified across both primes. The float64 'structural deficiency' was a numerical-precision artefact, not a genuine algebraic property. Consequence: H1's real content is NOT a difference in structural identifiability between hyperbolic and flat boundary-to-bulk inverse problems (both are exactly full rank at these sizes) -- it is a difference in CONDITIONING, i.e. the precision required to exploit that full rank, which grows polynomially (hyperbolic) vs super-polynomially, past float64's representable range by N~1000 (flat).
notes: experiments/track_h_hyperbolic_network/hyperbolic_exact.py (--self-test: 6/6 pass, including a cross-check of the modular rank against float64's trusted rank on the small {7,3} L=1 case). Not yet certified: N>475 for flat lattices (GF(p) Gaussian elimination on ~3500x1300 was the practical runtime limit reached in this session); full rank at N=475 is evidence against, not proof against, a deficiency appearing at some larger N. Any future prose using 'structurally unrecoverable' for the flat-lattice case must be corrected against this entry. statement: The bottom of the spectrum lambda_0 of the combinatorial Laplacian of an infinite graph of bounded degree is positive iff its edge-isoperimetric (Cheeger) constant is positive [Dodziuk, Trans. AMS 284 (1984) 787-794; Mohar, Linear Algebra Appl. 103 (1988) 119-131]; the {7,3} tiling graph has an explicit positive isoperimetric constant [Haggstrom, Jonasson & Lyons, Ann. Probab. 30 (2002) 443-473].
notes: Cited, not re-derived. Upper bound lambda_0 <= 3 - 2 sqrt 2 follows from the 3-regular tree covering. [evidence replaced: previous digest sha256:da41fda56922... hashed a literal string, not a file; now a JSON blob in docs/elenchus/evidence]

statement: For every tested {7,3} truncation, lambda_min(L_ii) is the Rayleigh-quotient minimum of the infinite {7,3} Laplacian over functions supported on the interior (by H2-B-0001), hence lambda_min(L_ii) >= lambda_0 > 0 and the RC relaxation time tau = C/lambda_min(L_ii) <= C/lambda_0 uniformly; since the interiors are nested and exhaust the tiling, lambda_min(L_ii) is non-increasing in L and converges to lambda_0. Flat disks have lambda_min -> 0.

Hypothesis, NOT tested: the matched filter combines all m^2 correlated matrix entries, giving a processing gain of order m over the single norm statistic used for detection (H3-X-0002), so localisation is limited only at much larger noise; the failure boundary needs a noise sweep. UPDATE (2026-09-28, appended; statement unchanged): the noise sweep H3-X-0006 shows the 60/60 result was a ceiling. The flat lattice fails at 3e-3 (x2) / 1e-3 (x1.25) while the hyperbolic holds to >= 1e-1, so 'no localisation advantage' holds only at the 3e-4 budget; the advantage is a noise-margin one.

statement: PREREGISTRATION_9 (localisation top-1 vs noise, deepest class, 20 trials per cell; eps_loc = largest grid noise keeping top-1 >= 0.9). S1 HELD: square R=10, x2: top-1 1.00 at 1e-3 and 0.00 at 1e-1, eps_loc 3e-3. S2 HELD: {7,3} L=3, x2: top-1 1.00 at 1e-2. S3 HELD: eps_loc ratio hyperbolic/flat >= 100 at N~316 for both contrasts (x2: > 3e-1 vs 0.003; x1.25: 0.1 vs 0.001), far above the 8-10x boundary-signal ratio (H3-X-0004). N~112: x2 0.1 vs 0.01; x1.25 0.03 vs 0.003. Quantitative miss: the matched-filter estimate put the hyperbolic x2 threshold near 3e-2; it never fails within the grid (>= 10x better). At the paper's 3e-4 budget the flat board has a 3-10x noise margin for localisation, the hyperbolic board >= 300x.
notes: experiments/track_h_hyperbolic_network/localize_noise.py. LIMITS: 20 trials, half-decade grid; the deepest class is one node on the square lattices; oracle dictionary, ideal board, i.i.d. noise. The >=100x ratio exceeds the signal ratio: hypothesis (untested) that separating neighbouring deep nodes, not raw amplitude, limits the flat lattice.

statement: PREREGISTRATION_10 (single-node localisation on random boards g=1+tau*U[-1,1], ideal-model dictionary, differential regime, deepest class, 20 trials per cell, 4 lattices x tau in (0.1, 1, 5)% x eps in (3e-4, 3e-3) x contrast in (1.25, 2) = 48 cells). T1 HELD (True): tau=0.1%, eps=3e-4, x2 localises perfectly on all four lattices. T2 REFUTED (False): square R=10 at tau=5%, eps=3e-4, x2 stays at top-1 1.00 (predicted < 0.9). T3 HELD (True): the hyperbolic lattice is never noticeably worse and leads by up to 0.45 (R10 x1.25, eps 3e-3). 45/48 cells are exactly 1.00; the only cells below 0.9 are square R=10 x1.25 at eps=3e-3 (R10 x1.25 at eps 3e-3: tau 0.1%/1%/5% = 0.6/0.6/0.55), the same value as on an ideal board within sampling error (0.50, H3-X-0006). notes: experiments/track_h_hyperbolic_network/localize_tolerance.py. LIMITS: tolerance up to 5% only (larger untested); noise 3e-4 and 3e-3 only; 20 trials (standard error ~0.11 near 0.5); single node on the square lattices' deepest class; oracle dictionary (known contrast set), single-node model, i.i.d. noise. Probable reason for the null effect, NOT tested: tolerance is common to the two maps of one board, so it cancels to first order in their difference; the model-based detection regime (H3-X-0003, B3) does not have this property.

statement: PREREGISTRATION_11 (log10 kappa of the DtN sensitivity Jacobian across (p,q) tilings via the closed-form Gram matrix in float64; gates passed: interior degree q in every tiling; controls v1.0 direct SVD {7,3} L=3 (diff 3e-12) and square R=6 (diff 1.1e-6, tolerance 3.1e-5 after Deviation 1). P1 HELD (True): log kappa is concave in L for {7,3} (increments 1.08, 0.81, 0.62) and {8,3} (0.96, 0.75, 0.63). P2 HELD (True): {8,3} is better conditioned than {7,3} at L = 2, 3, 4 (2.31 < 2.46, 3.06 < 3.27, 3.69 < 3.89). P3a HELD (True): at equal d_max the hyperbolic tilings agree within 0.45 (d_max=1), 0.25 (d_max=2), 0.56 (d_max=3), 0.21 (d_max=5) decades, while N varies by up to ~15x at fixed d_max. P3b HELD (True): at d_max = 5 square R=6 (5.07) and triangular R=6.45 (8.67) exceed the hyperbolic maximum (3.27) by >= 1.8 decades. P4 REFUTED (False): local exponents d log kappa / d log N between the two largest sizes are {8,3} 1.10 (<= 1.5 ok), {6,4} 0.98 (<= 1.0 ok), {5,4} 1.19 (> 1.0) and {4,5} 1.06 (> 1.0); they decrease with size but stay above 1 in the tested range. Reading: within the hyperbolic class log kappa is nearly a function of d_max alone and concave in it; across classes it is not (the flat lattice is linear in d_max and much worse at equal depth), so 'the mechanism is the scaling of depth with size' (paper v1.1, sec. 3.1) holds only within the hyperbolic class.
notes: experiments/track_h_hyperbolic_network/tilings_kappa.py. Unit conductances, full boundary only. Values carry a float64 error bound eps*kappa(G) (<= 4e-9 in log10 kappa for every hyperbolic tiling). Five tilings, <= 6 layers, N <= 2888; the (5,4), (6,4), (4,5) tilings reach d_max <= 4, so equal-d_max comparisons are limited to d_max <= 3 outside {7,3}/{8,3}.
